ranking.note: Raised to P1: a correctness bug where cached CheckBlock flags let blocks invalid under one chain's params pass under another is the only fund/consensus-correctness defect on this list.
Head of the logging chain; must be reviewed before #33847 and #30342, which depend on it.
Moved down five from its own score position: it is the last link of the logging chain and cannot be reviewed ahead of #34374 and #33847.

inconsistencies: Logging chain with a mandatory order: #34374 (structured log entries, drops logging.cpp from the kernel build) -> #33847 (attach connections to contexts) -> #30342 (route each context's output to its own connection). Reviewing them out of order wastes effort; #34374 first.

#34775 (make the logging callback global, delete btck_LoggingConnection handles because logging is really a singleton) points in the opposite direction from #33847/#30342 (make per-context logging connections real). These two designs cannot both land as written; a direction decision is needed, and the per-context branch carries the larger downstream chain, so review #34374/#33847 before spending time on #34775.

Four PRs restructure error propagation across the kernel boundary and overlap heavily: #29700 (util::Result/FlushResult returns for all fatal errors), #35646 (remove M_ERROR from ValidationState via util::Expected), #36326 (typed FatalError/FlushError instead of bilingual_str), #36318 (invalid states must carry a result, adds BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE). #29700 is the broadest and sets the return-value convention, so settle its approach first; #35646 is explicitly an RFC on the same ground.

#36318 adds a new enum value to ValidationState while #35646 removes the runtime-error state from it; whichever lands first forces a rebase of the other, so coordinate rather than review independently.

#36353, #29700, #35646 and #36318 substantively change validation logic as well as the kernel boundary; they are both kernel and validation PRs and may warrant splitting, with the validation half reviewed by validation reviewers.
#35662 is mostly a script/validation micro-optimization; only the fix for the unintended txdata copy in the C API is in-category, which is why it sits last.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: one correctness defect at the API boundary (P1), a solid P2 block of consumer-enabling features, boundary error propagation, build/library separation and the logging decoupling chain, then P3 API polish and documentation. Two distinct chains (logging, error propagation) dominate the P2 band and their internal order matters more than their relative scores.
